title: DataliVR: Transformation of Data Literacy Education through Virtual Reality with ChatGPT-Powered Enhancements
venue: IEEE International Symposium on Mixed and Augmented Reality (ISMAR 2024)
extended_summary:
This paper investigates whether an immersive virtual reality application, DataliVR, can improve data literacy learning for university students and whether adding a ChatGPT-powered conversational avatar changes learners’ experiences and outcomes. The core problem addressed is that traditional classroom approaches may not adequately support the multifaceted and applied nature of data literacy, particularly for data collection, cleaning, analysis, and visualization. The authors also note that the educational effects of integrating ChatGPT-based chatbots into VR learning environments remain underexplored.

The intervention was DataliVR, a custom VR learning environment that guides learners through a gamified data-literacy journey using a fruit-classification and machine-learning decision-tree context. The system included scenes for a fruit market introduction, data collection, data cleaning, data analysis, and data visualization. In the treatment condition, learners also had access to a ChatGPT-powered chatbot avatar using GPT-3.5 Turbo with speech-to-text and text-to-speech integration; in the comparison condition, the same VR experience was provided without the chatbot. Participants completed tasks, exercises, and quizzes in VR, and outcomes included user experience, system usability, motion sickness, task completion time, task accuracy, and quiz accuracy.

The study involved 30 university students from diverse academic backgrounds at the Technical University of Munich. Participants had no prior machine-learning knowledge and were randomly assigned to the chatbot or no-chatbot condition. The study took place in a VR lab, with an average intervention duration of about 23.23 minutes in a single session. There is no indication of teacher-mediated use; instead, students worked individually in a controlled lab environment with guided in-VR instructions.

The main conclusions are that DataliVR was generally usable and effective for supporting short-term data-literacy learning, with high user experience and usability ratings and reasonably strong task and quiz performance. The chatbot improved user experience and perceived usability, but unexpectedly did not improve learning performance; participants without the chatbot performed significantly better on task accuracy, while quiz differences were not significant. The authors conclude that ChatGPT-enhanced VR shows promise for improving learning experiences, but its influence on learning outcomes is more complex and requires further investigation.
quality_tier_rationale: This is an experimental between-subjects comparison with random assignment, but it is a small-sample university study (n=30) outside K-12 and without reported effect sizes or stronger causal reporting details needed for higher tiers. It provides some quantitative comparative evidence but has notable relevance and credibility limitations for the target framework.
impact_tier_rationale: The chatbot intervention improved user experience and usability perceptions, but it did not improve learning efficiency and was associated with significantly worse task performance relative to the no-chatbot condition. Because the AI component showed negative academic impact in the direct comparison, the overall intervention impact is best classified as red.

interventions.use_case: immersive VR gamified simulation for university students to learn data literacy through fruit data collection, cleaning, analysis, and visualization tasks.
ChatGPT-powered embodied conversational avatar integrated into the VR environment to provide on-demand personalized learning assistance during data literacy tasks.

finding.finding_summary: In a between-subjects experiment with 30 university students, DataliVR users showed relatively high overall learning performance in data-literacy task accuracy (M=0.79, SD=0.10) and quiz accuracy (M=0.73, SD=0.11), suggesting the VR simulation supported acquisition of data-literacy skills. However, when comparing chatbot conditions, participants without the ChatGPT chatbot outperformed those with the chatbot on task accuracy (M=0.83, SD=0.07 vs. M=0.75, SD=0.11), t(28)=2.26, p=.032, while quiz accuracy was also higher without the chatbot (M=0.75, SD=0.12 vs. M=0.71, SD=0.11) but not significantly so.
finding.measure: Interactive data-literacy task accuracy and in-VR quiz accuracy on data cleaning, analysis, and visualization-related knowledge
finding.effect_size: t(28)=2.26 for task accuracy comparison; quiz comparison not significant
finding.std_deviation: Task overall SD=0.10; quiz overall SD=0.11; without-chatbot task SD=0.07, with-chatbot task SD=0.11; without-chatbot quiz SD=0.12, with-chatbot quiz SD=0.11

finding.finding_summary: Participants reported high overall user experience in DataliVR (M=5.99, SD=0.58 on a 7-point scale), and the ChatGPT-enhanced version produced significantly better user experience than the no-chatbot version (M=6.24, SD=0.43 vs. M=5.75, SD=0.62), t(28)=-2.3, p=.028. Feedback in the chatbot condition suggested moderate overall positive chatbot experience (M=3.27, SD=0.64/5), with users rating the avatar as authentic (M=4.07, SD=0.83) and interaction as easy (M=3.93, SD=1.07), despite relatively infrequent use.
finding.measure: User Experience Questionnaire scores and chatbot experience ratings reflecting engagement, enjoyment, and perceived learning support
finding.std_deviation: Overall UX SD=0.58; with-chatbot SD=0.43; without-chatbot SD=0.62; chatbot feedback overall SD=0.64

finding.finding_summary: DataliVR task completion time was nearly identical across conditions: 22.56 minutes without the chatbot and 22.49 minutes with the chatbot when chatbot conversation time was excluded, with no significant difference reported. System usability was rated high overall (M=4.05, SD=0.36/5), and higher with the chatbot (M=4.19, SD=0.27 vs. M=3.91, SD=0.38), t(28)=-2.12, p=.044, but participants in the chatbot condition also reported significantly less confidence using the system without technical support on SUS item 4, U=159, p=.004.
finding.measure: Task completion time, System Usability Scale scores, and perceived need for technical support
finding.effect_size: t(28)=-2.12 for usability comparison; U=159 for technical-support item; time difference not significant
finding.std_deviation: Overall SUS SD=0.36; with-chatbot SD=0.27; without-chatbot SD=0.38
